text: welcome to race three of the Apex energy
summer series presented by Boon Chrysler
Dodge Jeep and RAM and this week we'll
be taking on the lone short track on the
schedule Iowa Speedway for 150 laps
let's hop straight into
qualifying whether you're dragging your
brakes or running full bore around the
outside the optimal angle of attack will
be all the same you want to dedicate
your first laps to getting your tires
warmed up without spinning once you get
up to speed I would recommend running
around the outside but with that said
the bumps in turn one can throw you into
the wall you may benefit from running a
lane lower as you get yourself ready for
your hot lap head back up to the outside
wall as you head into turns three and
four drag the brakes for a moment to
rotate the nose and Arc down half a lane
to build as much momentum as you can now
to turn four to take the White
Flag Trail break as you navigate your
wing to turn one get the nose pointed
toward the yellow line get back on the
gas once you feel the car begin to
rotate around the second pit exit line
the Wall comes up quickly though so if
you get back on the gas too soon you may
find yourself in it if you make it out
of turn two safely you'll want to
position yourself as wide as possible
and take a similar Arc and turns three
and four gently drag your brakes aim
with the yellow line with your left
front tire start easing back on the
throttle once you feel the car hook back
up if you nail it you'll track out to
the outside wall naturally as you make
your run to the Finish
Line this week the key to Victory will
be momentum running the inside and the
corners and tracking up to the walls in
the straightaways will be your best bet
if you're alone but if you're in a pack
of cars you'll want to place yourself
from the outside door of the car below
you it's easy to overshoot the corners
and square off your exits by mistake so
focus on rolling the center of the
corners to the best of your ability we
also have a few massive bumps on the
outside of turn one so you want to avoid
those at all costs they'll upset the car
and completely ruin your momentum if
you're not careful so you want to stay
below the dotted white line on that end
of the track in turns three and four
however every lane is fair game as the
Run goes on and the inside line begins
to heat up the outside may become the
preferred line so I would recommend
getting acquainted with it and finding
limits during practice with that being
said we still only have two sets of
tires in the pit so you may want to use
that outside line sparingly it pays off
if you use it properly but if you find
yourself overdriving corners and failing
to back up your entries your tires will
punish you for it if you stay patient
manage your tires and get the most out
of your green flag pit entry you'll have
a great shot toward the end of the race
especially if Tire strategy becomes a
factor good luck
